blocking.issue: Acceptance criterion 3 still fails. The earlier finding is resolved for this document and its depends_on files: the State client, telemetry, `/tap`, AI candidate, first-seen, Plugin key-rate and Semantic Cache counter rows are all present. The table still calls itself 'the complete inventory', but it leaves out per-Node in-memory state that sibling architecture documents define. For one of these items, losing it is not safe. Security and identity keeps the signed revocation list in memory only, and a detached restart forgets it. A Node restarted during a Ruralz Control outage therefore accepts revoked JWTs, API keys and `auth.basic` usernames again. That makes the closing sentence ('the worst outcome is an over-charged Quota or Token Budget and a few extra admissions per key') and SG-3 wrong. Other items are missing: the `auth.basic` success cache and username throttle buckets, where a restart refuses legitimate clients with RZ-AUTH-007 for 25 to 50 s; the per-Node trace-sampling token buckets (Observability); the 32 MiB automatic-persisted-query cache (Multi-protocol); and the event-ingress fetch buffers and uncommitted offsets (Multi-protocol), where a crash causes redelivery, so an Upstream can see a message twice. An operator reading this table cannot predict these restart effects, and the security effect is the most serious one.
blocking.evidence: Line 50: "This table is the complete inventory of in-memory per-Node state; new per-Node state needs a row here before it ships." Line 76: "So a Node can be killed at any instant: the worst outcome is an over-charged Quota or Token Budget and a few extra admissions per key." Line 39 (SG-3): "Losing a Node loses only its in-flight requests, connections and the state [Stateless data plane] lists". Security and identity, Revocation: "Ruralz Control delivers one signed revocation list to every Node of a Cluster, checked in memory" and "**Persistence.** A detached restart forgets entries (OQ-security-and-identity-5)". Security and identity, auth.basic Ramp: "A restart or Zero-Downtime Upgrade starts with an empty cache and LRU ... callers beyond the queue get RZ-AUTH-007 with `Retry-After` meanwhile". Observability: "Two per-Node token buckets admit sampled traces (target)". Multi-protocol: "Automatic persisted queries | Disposable Node-local cache bounded by bytes (P4) ... | 32 MiB per Node (target)" and "Consumer group; commit after settle".
blocking.fix: Add rows, each with a Bound, a Rebuilt from and a Why losing it is safe entry. (1) Revocation list: bound one signed list; rebuilt from the Control Stream, or from the watched entry file in file mode. The safety cell must state the gap honestly: "Not safe while detached: a restarted detached Node forgets revocations until Ruralz Control returns (OQ-security-and-identity-5); Planned (M2)". (2) `auth.basic` success cache and username buckets: 10,000 and 100,000 entries (target); rebuilt by re-verification at the hash rate; safe because no credential is admitted without a hash, but expect a ramp of 25 to 50 s (hypothesis) with RZ-AUTH-007 refusals. (3) Trace-sampling buckets: two per Node; refilled at start; at worst one burst of extra sampled traces. (4) Automatic persisted query cache: 32 MiB (target); rebuilt when clients re-register; clients retry with the full document. (5) Event-ingress fetch buffers and uncommitted offsets or unacked messages: bounded by `maxBufferedBytes`; rebuilt by broker redelivery; at-least-once delivery, so an Upstream may see a message twice. Then rewrite line 76 as: "the worst outcomes are an over-charged Quota or Token Budget, a few extra admissions per key, a re-verification ramp for `auth.basic`, redelivered ingress messages and, while detached, forgotten revocations (OQ-security-and-identity-5)". Also align SG-3.

In the countless-Node row, spell out 'plus the counted Nodes' share' as 'plus N_counted × max(1, 2 × `requests` / N_published)', so the formula stands on its own.
